q: How does architectural design relate to plumbing design?
o: The placement of the spaces determines the proper orientation of the plumbing layout
The location of the T&Bs, kitchen, laundry area and carport are critical in the accuracy of plumbing installation
Orientation of utilitarian spaces is vital to the efficiency of the plumbing system
n: Placing wet areas, the kitchen, laundry and carport well lets pipes run short and stack neatly, so all three statements hold.

q: The Plumbing System is generally understood to comprise which two systems?
o: Water Supply and Storm Drainage System
n: A plumbing system has two sides: the water supply that brings clean water in, and the drainage that takes waste and storm water out.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: Which of these is NOT a plumbing appliance?
n: An appliance is equipment with a special plumbing function that uses or treats water: washers, heaters, ice makers. A faucet is a fitting that only lets water out.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: Which item below would NOT be considered a plumbing appurtenance?
n: Appurtenances are parts that go with fixtures, like shower heads, faucets and soap dishes. A washing machine is an appliance.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: Among these, which one is NOT categorized as a plumbing fixture?
n: Bidets, floor drains and lavatories receive water and discharge waste, so they are fixtures. A shower valve is a fitting that controls flow.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: The National Plumbing Code of the Philippines is enforced and administered by whom?
n: The plumbing code names the Administrative Authority, the local Plumbing Official, as the one who enforces it.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: Under PD 198, who heads the Local Water Utilities Administration (LWUA)?
o: The Secretary of Public Works and Highways
n: PD 198 made LWUA a government corporation run by a Board of Trustees and an Administrator. The Plumbing Official enforces the plumbing code locally, a different job.
ref: PD 198 — Provincial Water Utilities Act of 1973

q: The acronym MWSS stands for which agency?
n: MWSS is the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System. Since 1997 it has let concessions to Manila Water (East) and Maynilad (West).

q: The overall Drainage System is composed of which two subsystems?
o: Sanitary Drainage System and Storm Drainage System
Sanitary System and Non-Potable Water Supply
n: Drainage has two parts: sanitary drainage for waste from fixtures, and storm drainage for rain.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: In designing a PWD-accessible toilet, which requirements must be strictly followed?
n: An accessible toilet must meet all three: cubicle size, door clear width, and lavatory height.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the minimum floor area of an accessible toilet cubicle?
n: 1.80 m × 1.80 m = 3.24 m². The 1994 IRR size of 1.70 × 1.80 m gave 3.06 m².

q: What term describes plumbing work carried out before fixtures are set or finishes applied?
n: Roughing-in is placing pipes, vents and outlets inside walls and floors before fixtures and finishes go on.

q: Which allied professional is recognized for performing plumbing works?
n: RA 1378 limits plumbing design and supervision to Registered Master Plumbers.
ref: RA 1378 — Plumbing Law of the Philippines

q: Under the plumbing code, what makes up one "plumbing unit"?
o: One water closet and one lavatory, with a single floor drain and one hose bibb
A WC, lavatory, kitchen sink, shower, laundry tray and water meter, plus 3 floor drains and 4 faucets
A water closet, a lavatory and a shower, all served by one common trap
Any group of fixtures that discharges into a single vent stack
n: The plumbing unit is the minimum standard set of fixtures for a dwelling: one each of water closet, lavatory, kitchen sink, shower head, laundry tray and water meter, plus three floor drains and four faucets or hose bibbs.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: Which characteristic best defines what constitutes a building?
n: A building is a structure meant for human habitation or occupancy. That is what sets it apart from other structures.

q: What gives a toilet-and-bath natural ventilation to clear shower moisture, without mechanical equipment?
n: A window to the outside is the natural way to vent moisture. Fans and dehumidifiers work too, but they are mechanical and need power.
ref: NBC IRR — Rule VIII, light and ventilation

q: Which side of a tropical house plan is usually given to service areas like the laundry and kitchen?
o: The west, where the hot afternoon sun falls
The east, to catch the morning sun
The north, for steady, glare-free daylight
n: West sun is the hottest and hardest to shade, so service areas are put there as a buffer. Bedrooms and living areas go on the cooler east and north.

q: In a tropical house plan, which rooms are best placed on the east side?
o: The kitchen and laundry, which need the hottest sun
Bedrooms, which get gentle morning sun and cool down by night
The garage and storage, which need no daylight
The service stair and utility room
n: Morning sun on the east is mild and wakes the rooms up, and those rooms have cooled again by bedtime. Service areas take the harsh west sun instead.

q: What is an open, unoccupied space on the same lot as a building, bounded on two or more sides by the building's walls?
n: A court is open to the sky and bounded by the building's walls. An atrium is a covered space inside the building, and a setback is the required distance from the property line.

q: What property makes water considered potable?
n: Potable water is safe to drink. Clarity, treatment or filtering alone do not prove that.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What makes water non-potable?
o: It is not fit for drinking or cooking
It has been treated with chlorine
It has been filtered through sand and gravel
It looks clear but has not been tested
n: Non-potable water is unsafe to drink. Chlorination and filtration are ways of making water potable, not signs that it is not.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: Rivers, lakes and seas are what kind of water source?
n: Surface water is open to the air. Ground water is held in the soil and rock below, and storm water is the runoff from rain.

q: What do you call water that stands in or moves through the ground?
n: Ground water fills the pores of soil and rock below the water table and is drawn out by wells.

q: If water is sourced from a communal faucet system, what level of water service does this represent?
n: Level I is a point source such as a well, Level II is a communal faucet system, and Level III is a household tap off a piped network.

q: Which water treatment process uses a granular medium such as sand, crushed anthracite coal, or activated carbon?
n: Filters pass water through beds of sand, anthracite or activated carbon to trap fine particles.

q: What is chlorine mainly added to drinking water for?
n: Chlorine kills bacteria and viruses and leaves a residual that keeps protecting the water in the pipes.

q: Which two minerals in well water cause reddish-brown and black stains on fixtures and laundry?
n: Iron leaves rust-colored stains and manganese leaves black ones. Calcium and magnesium cause hardness, which shows up as white scale.

q: Which of these is another name for a bibb or faucet?
n: Bibb, faucet, tap and cock all name the valve at the end of a line. A plug closes an opening; a union and a coupling join pipes.

q: Which type of faucet is designed for use at a pantry sink?
n: A gooseneck faucet's tall, curved spout leaves room to fill pots and pails at a pantry sink.

q: A pipe installed with a 2% slope is classified as what type of pipe?
n: Drainage pipes that run nearly level are laid at about 2% (1:50) so waste keeps flowing. Stacks and risers run vertically.

q: A six-storey building has no elevated water tank. What water supply arrangement is being used?
n: Without an elevated tank, water is pumped from a cistern into a pressure tank that feeds the floors. That is the indirect upfeed arrangement.

q: Which pump type, using a spinning impeller, is the usual choice for lifting water in high-rise buildings?
n: Centrifugal pumps give steady flow at high capacity, and multistage units reach the head a tall building needs.

q: Which water heater uses roof panels to warm water with sunlight, often with an electric backup?
n: Solar collectors heat water that is kept in an insulated tank. An electric or gas booster covers cloudy days.

q: When water is drawn straight from the main line without intermediate storage, this is called?
n: In direct upfeed, the main's own pressure pushes water up to the fixtures, with no tank in between. It suits low buildings only.

q: What do you call the system where water goes indirectly from the main to an elevated tank, then flows down by gravity?
n: Water is pumped from a cistern to an elevated tank, then flows down to the fixtures by gravity.

q: In which application are submersible pumps typically installed?
n: A submersible pump sits under water at the bottom of a well and pushes water up.

q: What causes the banging sound heard inside pipes?
n: Water hammer is the bang from a pressure surge when flowing water stops suddenly, as when a valve snaps shut.

q: Which device, a capped vertical pipe holding air, is installed to cushion water hammer?
n: The trapped air in an air chamber compresses and absorbs the surge when a valve slams shut. Factory-made arrestors do the same job with a sealed piston.

q: Which valve stops flow using a circular disk positioned at right angles to the flow direction?
n: A gate valve lowers a flat gate across the flow. It is meant to be fully open or fully closed, not for throttling.

q: Which valve opens on its own to release pressure from a boiler or water heater once a safe limit is passed?
n: A relief valve is spring-loaded and opens automatically at its set pressure. A blow-off valve is opened by hand to flush sediment out.

q: Which valve prevents water from flowing back in reverse?
n: A check valve has a swing disc or spring-loaded poppet that flow pushes open and backflow pushes shut.

q: Which valve type is used specifically for throttling (regulating) water flow?
n: A globe valve's disc closes onto a seat across an S-shaped path, which makes fine control of flow easy.

q: Which pipe system has no permanent connection to a water supply?
n: A dry standpipe has no water until the fire department pumps into it through the Siamese connection.

q: A cast iron pipe made without a hub is called what?
n: Hubless cast iron has plain ends joined by a neoprene gasket and stainless steel clamp.

q: Which plastic pipe is commonly used for both cold-water supply lines and sanitary drainage lines?
n: Unplasticized PVC comes in pressure grades for water and in thinner grades for drainage. Copper and GI are for water supply, and cast iron is for drainage.

q: Which jointing method is used for HDPE pipes?
n: HDPE is joined by melting: electrofusion fittings have built-in heating wires, and butt fusion heats the pipe ends. Solvent cement does not bond polyethylene.

q: How is a bell-and-spigot cast iron soil pipe joint traditionally made?
o: Threaded and sealed with pipe dope
Packed with oakum, then sealed with molten lead
Fused with an electric heating coil
n: Oakum is packed into the bell, then molten lead is poured and caulked tight. Hubless cast iron uses a neoprene sleeve and steel clamp instead.

q: What fitting, threaded on the inside, is used to join two straight lengths of pipe?
n: A coupling has inside threads on both ends and joins two pipes in a straight line.

q: What fitting, threaded on the outside, is used to join two straight lengths of pipe?
n: A nipple is a short piece of pipe with outside threads on both ends.

q: Which fitting, threaded on the inside, is used to close off the end of a pipe?
n: A cap screws over the outside threads of a pipe end, so it is threaded on the inside.

q: Which fitting, threaded on the outside, is used to close off the end of a pipe?
n: A plug screws into an inside-threaded fitting, so it is threaded on the outside.

q: What fitting joins the service pipe to the distribution pipe?
n: A union patente (union) joins the service pipe to the distribution piping and can be undone to remove the meter or valve.

q: What do you call the two-gated outlet fitting used for dry and wet standpipes?
n: A Siamese connection has two inlets so fire trucks can pump into a standpipe or sprinkler system.

q: What process is used to connect a pipe's spigot end into the bell end?
n: The spigot end sits in the bell and is sealed by caulking: packed oakum topped with lead.

q: What method is used to join copper water tubes?
n: Copper is joined by soldering with a torch, or by brazing for higher strength. Electrofusion is for polyethylene, and solvent cement is for PVC.

q: What term covers the construction, collection, transport, pumping, treatment, and final disposal of sewage?
n: Sewerage covers the whole sewer system: collecting, carrying, pumping, treating and disposing of sewage.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What is the term for an underground drainage system that cannot drain by gravity into the building sewer?
n: A building subdrain is below the sewer level, so its waste must be lifted by a sump or ejector.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: Which pipe begins where the building drain ends?
n: The building sewer (house sewer) starts 0.6 m outside the wall, where the building drain ends, and runs to the public sewer.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What system of piping carries waste water from plumbing fixtures to the sewer?
n: The drainage system is all the piping that carries waste water from fixtures to the sewer or disposal point.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What is the lowest horizontal drainage pipe inside a building, which carries waste to a point 0.6 m outside the wall?
n: The building drain collects from the soil and waste stacks and runs to 0.6 m outside the foundation wall. From there the building (house) sewer takes over.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What is the pipe called that runs from the building to the public storm sewer system?
n: The house storm sewer carries rain water from the building to the public storm sewer.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What do you call the drain running from a fixture's trap to the point where it joins another drain?
n: The fixture drain runs from a fixture's trap to where it joins another drain pipe.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What is a waste pipe called when it does not connect directly to the building drainage system?
n: An indirect waste pipe discharges through an air gap into a receptor, so sewage cannot back up into it.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What is the runoff from rain on roofs and paved areas called in plumbing?
n: Storm water is carried by gutters, leaders and storm drains. Gray water comes from sinks and showers, and sewage from water closets.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What structure retains liquids long enough to let settleable material deposit out?
n: A catch basin holds water long enough for sand and grit to settle before the water flows on.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What term describes an interceptor with a capacity of 3 cubic meters?
n: A grease interceptor holds up to 3.0 m³ and serves a whole kitchen. A grease trap is small and serves one to four fixtures.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What is the vertical depth of water held in a trap, between its dip and its crown weir?
n: The trap seal (water seal) blocks sewer gas. The code requires a seal of 50 to 100 mm; deeper seals trap solids.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What is the principal artery of the vent system, to which vent branches connect?
n: The main vent is the trunk that branch vents join. It runs to the roof or joins the stack vent above the highest fixture.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What term refers to providing air flow to and from a drainage system, circulating air to protect trap seals from siphonage and back pressure?
n: The vent system brings air into the drainage piping so trap seals are not siphoned or blown out.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What do you call a pipe or opening that ensures air circulates through a plumbing system, reducing pressure on trap seals?
n: A vent pipe is any pipe or opening that lets air circulate in the drainage system.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What venting arrangement allows a single vent pipe to serve two traps?
n: A unit (common) vent joins two fixture drains at the same level and vents both traps.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: Which type of vent functions as an auxiliary vent, also known as a 'yoke vent'?
n: A relief vent lets air move between the drainage and vent systems. A yoke vent is a relief vent from a soil stack to the vent stack.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What watertight tank separates solids from liquid, digests organic matter, and lets the clarified liquid flow on to a leaching field or seepage pit?
n: A septic tank must be watertight, and its effluent goes into the soil through open-jointed pipes or a seepage pit. A cesspool is not watertight and lets raw sewage seep out.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What is waste made up of human excrement and liquid household waste called?
n: Sanitary sewage contains human waste. Gray water is only from sinks, showers and laundry, without toilet waste.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: Which term names the pipe connecting a building to the public storm sewer system?
n: The house storm sewer carries storm water from the building to the public storm sewer.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What term names an outhouse or structure built for the deposit of excrement?
n: A privy is an outhouse over a pit, used where there is no water-carried sewage system.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions

q: What is the minimum distance between a septic tank and a water supply well?
n: The siting table of the plumbing code sets 15.20 m from wells and streams, 1.50 m from buildings and property lines, and 3.00 m from trees and pressure water mains.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code, Table B-1 (siting of septic tanks)

q: What is the minimum number of chambers required in a Septic Tank?
n: A septic tank needs at least two compartments: the inlet one holds 2/3 of the volume, the second 1/3.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions, private sewage disposal

q: What is the minimum length of the first (inlet) compartment of a septic tank?
n: The inlet compartment must be at least 1.50 m long and 0.90 m wide, hold at least 2/3 of the tank, and have a liquid depth of 0.60 to 1.80 m.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions, private sewage disposal

q: In the absence of a public sewer, what should be installed?
n: Where there is no public sewer, sewage goes to a septic tank. Cesspools are no longer allowed for new work.
ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RA 1378), definitions, private sewage disposal

q: For a deep well, which pump is most suitable for lifting water up to the potable water cistern?
n: A submersible pump sits in the deep well and pushes water up to the cistern. Surface pumps cannot lift water from deep wells.

q: Among the illustrations, which figure represents a Piston Pump?
n: Pump B is a reciprocating (piston) pump driven by a belt and flywheel.

q: Which figure among the illustrations shows a Centrifugal Pump?
n: Pump A is an end-suction centrifugal pump: a motor coupled to a volute casing.

q: Which of the illustrated figures depicts a Sump Pump?
n: Pump D is a sump pump. Its float switch starts it when water in the pit rises.

q: Which figure among the illustrations corresponds to a Submersible Pump?
n: Pump C is a slim borehole submersible pump, made to fit down a well casing.

q: Among the figures shown, which one represents a Jockey Pump?
n: Pump E is a small vertical multistage pump, used as a jockey pump to keep a fire line pressurized.

q: For a residential kitchen, which fire detection device best minimizes false alarms from steam and cooking fumes while still responding promptly to a slow-developing appliance fire?
n: Photoelectric detectors respond well to smoldering fires and are less set off by steam and cooking fumes than ionization types.

q: In a multi-unit residential condominium, which detection device is typically installed in bedrooms, corridors, and common areas to give early warning of smoldering or flaming fires?
n: Smoke detectors warn earliest for both smoldering and flaming fires, so they go in sleeping areas and corridors.

q: Which smoke detector type uses a small amount of radioactive material between charged plates, triggering an alarm when smoke disrupts the current flow, and is now banned in some areas?
n: Ionization detectors use a tiny radioactive source between charged plates. Smoke lowers the current and triggers the alarm.

q: Which type of lighting produces soft, evenly scattered light without harsh shadows by reflecting off ceilings and walls, making it suited for general illumination?
n: Indirect lighting bounces off ceilings and walls, giving soft light with few shadows.

q: Which lighting type sends light straight from the fixture to the surface without diffusion, producing sharp shadows and high contrast, as seen in downlights, floodlights, and pendants?
n: Direct lighting sends light straight down from the fixture, giving sharp shadows.

q: Which lighting type provides focused, brighter illumination for activities like reading, cooking, or working?
n: Task lighting gives brighter light exactly where work is done, such as a desk or counter.

q: Which lighting type is used to draw visual emphasis to architectural features, artwork, or decor through focused illumination?
n: Accent lighting uses focused beams to highlight artwork or architectural features.

q: Which lighting layer gives a room its overall, comfortable brightness and is the base of a layered lighting design?
n: Ambient (general) lighting comes first. Task lighting is added where people work, and accent lighting highlights features.

q: Which control, usually mounted about 1.07 m (42 in) above the floor in the lobby, is pressed to summon an elevator?
n: Hall call buttons are outside the car, with an up and a down button. The car operating panel with floor buttons is inside the car.

q: Which lobby device lights an arrow and chimes to show which car is arriving and in which direction?
n: Hall lanterns are mounted over or beside each hoistway door, so waiting passengers can move to the right car.

q: Which elevator door travels with the car and opens and closes at each floor?
n: The car door drives the hoistway door open when the car is level with a floor. Each floor has its own hoistway door.

q: Which elevator door stays at each floor and keeps people from falling into the shaft when the car is not there?
n: Hoistway doors can only open when the car is at that floor, and they are interlocked so the car cannot move with one open.

q: Which device on the elevator car door reopens it when it touches or senses a passenger in the doorway?
n: A safety edge or light curtain stops and reverses the closing door. The governor and buffer protect against overspeed and overtravel, not door strikes.

q: Referring to the figures shown, what is Figure A, a component used in LED lighting?
n: Figure A is an LED driver. It turns mains AC into the low-voltage DC that LEDs need.

q: Referring to the figures above, what is the typical application of the fixture shown in Figure B?
n: Figure B is an in-ground uplight, set flush in paving or lawn to light walls and trees from below.

q: Looking at the figures above, which lamp type is illustrated in Figure C?
n: Figure C is an LED bulb. The ribbed neck is its heat sink.

q: Based on the figures shown, which of the lamp types qualify as energy-saving lighting?
n: The LED bulb (C) and the compact fluorescents (D) use far less energy than incandescent lamps.

q: Which component must be paired with the lamp in Figure D for it to operate?
n: Compact fluorescent lamps need a ballast to start and limit current. Screw-in CFLs have an electronic ballast built into the base.

q: In the duct figure, what does the component labelled A do?
o: Removes unwanted air from inside to outside of the building
Brings conditioned air to any part of the building
Stops or regulates airflow within the ductwork
Serves as a commercial or industrial-grade exhaust duct
n: Figure A is a motorized damper: a blade inside the duct turns to stop or regulate airflow.

q: In the illustration, what device is shown as Figure B?
n: Figure B is a solar attic fan. Its panel runs a fan that pulls hot air out of the roof space.

q: What term describes the fitting placed at the terminal end of a duct run to spread conditioned air evenly across a room?
n: A diffuser, like Figure C, spreads supply air evenly into the room at the end of a duct run.

q: What is the box-shaped outdoor equipment with a top-discharge fan shown as Figure D?
n: The fan grille on top and the coil louvers on the sides mark it as an air-conditioning unit that rejects heat outdoors.

q: Which device is built specifically to reduce noise carried through air ducts?
n: A sound attenuator is a duct section lined with absorptive baffles. Dampers control airflow or fire spread, not noise.

q: Which bathtub type is set against three walls, with a finished apron only on its open side?
n: The recessed tub fits an alcove and saves space. A freestanding or clawfoot tub is finished all around, and a drop-in tub sits in a built deck.

q: Which of the following are all recognized faucet brands?
n: Grohe, Delta and Moen are all faucet brands.

q: Which brand is known for manufacturing cordless telephones?
n: Panasonic makes cordless telephones. Aiphone makes intercoms, Fumaco makes lighting, and Belden makes cable.

q: Which of these is a manufacturer of lavatories and water closets, not a hardware retailer?
n: Duravit is a German sanitary-ware maker. Wilcon, Citi Hardware and Handyman are Philippine retail chains that sell many brands.

q: Which brand is known for CCTV cameras and recorders?
n: Hikvision makes security cameras and NVRs. Schneider makes breakers and switchgear, Atlanta makes pipes, and Phelps Dodge makes wires.

q: Which company is a well-known Philippine maker of building wires and cables?
n: Phelps Dodge Philippines makes THHN and other building wire. Philips is known for lighting, and Schneider for switchgear.

q: Which company is a well-known maker of network cables such as Cat 6?
n: Belden makes data and signal cable. Moen, Grohe and Duravit make plumbing fixtures.

q: What box breaks a long conduit run into shorter pulling sections and holds no splices?
n: Pull boxes are placed where a run is long or has many bends. A junction box is where conductors are spliced or tapped.

q: Which conduit is thin-walled, unthreaded, and joined with set-screw or compression fittings?
n: EMT is light and easy to bend, used in exposed indoor work. IMC and RSC are thicker and threaded, for heavier protection.

q: What is the term for a box that safeguards wire splices and taps?
n: A junction box encloses splices and taps so they are protected and can be reached later.

q: Referring to the figure set above, which drain type would you specify for a driveway or garage area?
n: Drain C is a heavy grating, strong enough for car wheels on a driveway or garage floor.

q: Which of the illustrated drain types above is appropriate for a bathroom shower floor?
n: Drain D is a linear shower drain, a long slotted channel set in a shower floor.

q: Which drain is installed at a roof or gutter outlet, with a dome strainer to keep leaves out?
n: Drain A is a dome roof drain. The raised strainer lets water in even when debris collects around it.

q: Which drain passes through a roof-deck parapet wall, draining water out sideways?
n: Drain B is a parapet (scupper) drain with a side outlet. It sits at deck level where the parapet meets the slab.

q: Which item is a cleanout plug, removed to reach and clear a blocked drain line?
n: Item E is a threaded brass cleanout plug with a square head for a wrench. Cleanouts are required at the base of stacks and at changes of direction.

q: What do you call the device — also known as a position indicator — that tells waiting passengers an elevator is arriving and which direction it will travel?
n: The hall indicator, or position indicator, shows where the car is and which way it is going.

q: Which of these home appliances usually draws the most power?
n: An instant water heater draws about 3,500 to 6,000 W. A fan draws about 50 W, a refrigerator about 100 to 200 W, and an LED TV about 100 W.

q: A 1,500 W hair dryer is used 20 minutes a day for 30 days. How much energy does it use?
n: Energy is power times time. Convert watts to kilowatts and minutes to hours first.
steps: Hours of use: 20 min × 30 days = 600 min = 10 h

q: An electric fan is rated 60 W on a 230 V line. About how much current does it draw?
n: For a resistive or near-unity power factor load, current is power divided by voltage.

q: Which appliance should be given its own individual branch circuit because of its large load?
n: Air conditioners, water heaters and ranges get individual circuits so their load does not trip or overload a shared outlet circuit.

q: A 1.5 kW air conditioner runs on 230 V. About how much current does it draw?
n: A 2-hp class unit on 230 V draws a few amperes. The branch circuit is then sized with margin for the starting current.

q: Per the Philippine Green Building Code, what is the maximum allowable dual-flush volume, in liters, for a water closet?
n: Dual-flush water closets may use at most 6 L for a full flush and 3 L for a low flush.
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Table 13 and Sec. on escalators

q: Under the Philippine Green Building Code, what is the maximum single-flush water consumption, in liters, allowed for a water closet?
n: Single-flush water closets may use at most 4.9 L per flush.
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Table 13 and Sec. on escalators

q: What is the maximum permitted flow rate, in liters, for urinal fixtures?
n: Urinals may use at most 1 L per flush.
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Table 13 and Sec. on escalators

q: After how long a period of no detected activity must escalators and moving ramps automatically slow down, at most, under the automated control requirement?
n: Escalators and moving ramps must slow down after at most 1½ minutes with no activity.
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Table 13 and Sec. on escalators

q: What is the maximum period of inactivity before an escalator or moving ramp must automatically switch to standby mode?
n: Escalators and moving ramps must go to standby after at most 5 minutes with no activity.
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Table 13 and Sec. on escalators

q: When conveying storm water to the public main line, which method is generally the most cost-effective and simplest to maintain?
n: An open concrete culvert costs little and is easy to clean, compared with buried pipes that need manholes.

q: In the set of illustrations above, what is the drainage feature labeled A?
n: A is a swale: a shallow, grassed channel that carries and soaks up runoff.

q: Which drainage element is shown as B in the illustrations?
n: B is a precast concrete culvert: pipes laid under a road or fill to carry water through.

q: In the illustrations above, what feature is labeled D?
n: D is a wingwall: the angled walls at a culvert's mouth that hold back the soil and guide the flow.

q: What term refers to the combined direct and indirect sunlight available during daytime hours?
n: Daylight is all the light from the sky in the day, both direct sun and diffuse skylight.

q: Which light quality has a higher blue content and appears brighter to the human eye?
n: Cool light, about 5,000 K and up, has more blue and looks brighter and crisper.

q: Which light description typically ranges through shades of red, orange, and yellow?
n: Warm light, about 2,700 to 3,000 K, has red, orange and yellow tones.

q: Which type of light would you specify for a kitchen space?
n: Cool light shows food colors and cleanliness clearly, so it suits kitchen work.

q: Which lighting fixture type is the best recommendation for kitchen use?
n: LEDs are efficient, last long and give little heat, which suits kitchens.

q: Which insulation is made by spinning molten volcanic rock into fibers?
n: Rockwool is spun from basalt. Glass wool is spun from glass. Both are mineral wools that insulate against heat and sound and do not burn.

q: Which insulation is non-combustible and both thermally and acoustically effective?
n: Mineral wool (rockwool or glass wool) resists fire and absorbs sound. Polystyrene foam burns, and treated cellulose is only fire-retardant.

q: What insulation material is formed by binding glass fibers into a wool-like texture?
n: Glass wool is spun from molten glass and bonded into a soft, yellow batt.

q: Figure B is a batt spun from basalt rock. What is it?
n: Rockwool is brownish-green and denser than glass wool. It is used in fire-rated and acoustic walls.

q: The materials in Figures A, B and C all belong to which family of insulation?
n: Glass wool and rockwool are both mineral wools. Only Figure D, gypsum drywall, is a board rather than a fibrous insulation.

q: Which figure in the illustration set represents Glass Wool?
n: Figure A is glass wool: yellow, soft, and faced with foil here.

q: Which of the illustrated figures shows Drywall?
n: Figure D is gypsum drywall, stacked sheets with paper faces.

q: Which fixture is a high-bay lamp suited to an 8-meter-high ceiling?
n: High-bay fixtures have a deep reflector that throws light down from 6 m or more. They are used in warehouses, factories and supermarkets.

q: Which fixture is a recessed, adjustable downlight that needs a cut-out in the ceiling?
n: Fixture C has gimbal heads set into a ceiling plate, so each lamp can be aimed at walls or displays.

q: Which fixture has two lamp heads that switch on from a battery when the power fails?
n: Fixture A is an emergency light. It charges from the mains and lights exits and stairs during an outage.

q: Which fixture in the illustration is best suited for outdoor commercial applications?
n: The floodlight (Fixture D) is weatherproof and made for outdoor commercial use.

q: Which of the fixtures shown is mandated by the building code?
n: Emergency lights (Fixture A) are required by the Fire Code along exits and stairs.
ref: Fire Code of the Philippines — emergency lighting

q: Which fixture pictured would you use to highlight a building's facade?
n: The floodlight (Fixture D) is aimed up at a facade to wash it with light.

q: Which of the illustrated fixtures comes with a built-in battery?
n: Emergency lights (Fixture A) carry a rechargeable battery that runs them in an outage.

q: Which fixture is a flexible LED strip used for cove and accent lighting?
n: Fixture B is a strip or tape light. It can be cut to length and hidden in coves, shelves and bar counters.

q: Which fixture is a floodlight, fixed on a U-bracket so it can be aimed?
n: Fixture D is an LED floodlight in a sealed housing. It lights facades, signs, yards and parking areas.

q: Which fixture shown would typically light a supermarket?
n: High-bays (Fixture E) light supermarkets, with their high open ceilings.

q: Which of the illustrated fixtures is used to light a stairway?
n: Emergency lights (Fixture A) are placed in stairways so people can find their way out.

q: Which figure depicts a fixture meant for exterior use?
n: The floodlight (Fixture D) has a sealed, weatherproof housing for exterior use.

q: Which two fixtures would typically be used in a bar lounge or club?
n: Strip lights (B) and adjustable downlights (C) give low, focused, moody light. Floodlights and high-bays are too harsh.

q: Which two fixtures would be found in a warehouse?
n: A warehouse needs high-bays (E) for its tall ceiling and emergency lights (A) along its exits.

q: What lighting product — also called tape or ribbon light — is flexible, cuttable to length, and suited for both indoor and outdoor use?
n: Strip lights are flexible LED tapes that can be cut to length.

q: What is the process of treating air to control its temperature, humidity, cleanliness and distribution at the same time?
n: Air conditioning does all four at once. Ventilation only exchanges air, and refrigeration only removes heat.

q: In air-conditioning schedules, what does WACU stand for?
n: A WACU is a single box set in a window or wall opening, with the evaporator facing in and the condenser facing out.

q: The indoor component of an air conditioning system is known as what?
n: The evaporator coil sits indoors and absorbs heat from the room air.

q: What is the outdoor coil of an air-conditioning system, where heat is rejected, called?
n: In the condenser the hot refrigerant gas gives up heat to the outside air and turns back into liquid. The evaporator absorbs heat indoors.

q: In a split-type air conditioner, what is the outdoor condensing unit called in schedules?
n: ACCU means air-cooled condensing unit. It holds the compressor, condenser coil and fan.

q: In a split-type air conditioner, what is the indoor evaporator unit usually called?
n: The indoor unit is a fan blowing room air across a cooling coil, so it is a fan coil unit. The ACCU sits outside.

q: In a chilled-water system, which unit cools a single room using chilled water from a central chiller?
n: FCUs sit in each room and take chilled water from the plant. Larger zones use air handling units with ducts.

q: What term describes using operable windows to achieve natural ventilation?
n: Passive cooling uses the building itself, such as windows, shading and cross ventilation, with no machines.

q: What is it called when mechanical equipment is used to provide artificial ventilation?
n: Active cooling uses powered equipment such as fans and air conditioners.

q: What minimum floor-to-ceiling height applies to spaces relying on natural ventilation?
n: Naturally ventilated rooms need at least 2.70 m ceilings so warm air can rise above people.

q: What is the required floor-to-ceiling height for spaces served by artificial (mechanical) ventilation?
n: Mechanically ventilated rooms may have ceilings as low as 2.40 m.

q: Why should the refrigerant piping between the indoor and outdoor units of a split AC be kept short?
o: Long runs make the unit colder than rated
Long runs lose pressure and cut capacity
Short runs are required only for looks
Long runs make the compressor quieter
n: Every metre of line set adds friction and heat gain. Makers publish a maximum length and height difference for each model.

q: Which of the following is NOT actually a component of a split-type air conditioning system?
n: A split system has an ACCU outdoors, an indoor unit (AHU or FCU), and a condensate pipe. FHU is not a component.

q: Where is a cassette-type air conditioning unit installed?
n: A cassette unit is set into the ceiling and blows air out on four sides.

q: What is another name for a package-type unit within a split air conditioning system?
n: A package unit is a floor-mounted, freestanding cabinet.

q: What term describes a sound wave bending, or "flowing," around an obstacle or through an opening?
n: Diffraction is sound bending around obstacles and spreading through openings.

q: What is the name of the value representing the fraction of randomly incident sound power that gets absorbed rather than reflected?
n: The sound absorption coefficient (SAC) runs from 0 (all reflected) to 1 (all absorbed).

q: Which ceiling shape is used to diffuse sound?
n: Splayed and convex surfaces scatter sound evenly. Concave domes and vaults focus it into hot spots.

q: What is the term for the scattering, or random redistribution, of a sound wave off a surface?
n: Diffusion scatters sound evenly in many directions off an uneven surface.

q: Which term means blocking sound from passing from one room into another?
n: Isolation uses mass, airtightness and separation to stop sound going through a wall. Absorption only reduces reflected sound within a room.

q: Which term means turning sound energy into heat inside a porous material, reducing reflections within the same room?
n: Porous absorbers like mineral wool cut echo and reverberation, but they are light and do little to stop sound passing through a wall.

q: What single-number index is used to rate a material's sound-absorptive performance?
n: NRC is the average of the absorption coefficients at 250, 500, 1,000 and 2,000 Hz.

q: What decibel-based value is obtained by comparing sound pressure levels at a given frequency between the source room and the receiving room?
n: Transmission loss (TL) is the drop in sound level, in dB, from one room through a wall to the next.

q: What shape reflects sound toward two separate focal points?
n: An ellipse reflects sound from one focus to the other, as in whispering galleries.

q: What shape concentrates reflected sound onto a single focal point?
n: A parabola reflects incoming parallel sound to a single focal point.

q: What term describes a distinct sound reflection perceived with both loudness and a noticeable time delay?
n: An echo is a distinct reflection heard at least about 1/20 s after the direct sound.

q: What phenomenon results from sound repeatedly bouncing between hard, parallel surfaces?
n: Flutter echo is a rapid buzz of reflections between two hard parallel surfaces.

q: What single-number rating expresses how well a material or assembly blocks sound transmission?
n: STC rates how well a wall or floor blocks airborne sound. Higher is better.

q: Which of the following has the lowest STC (sound transmission class) rating?
n: An empty stud cavity lets sound resonate through, so it has the lowest STC of these.

q: Which change raises the STC of a stud wall the most?
o: Painting the wall with a thick coat of paint
Hanging framed pictures on both sides
Leaving the stud cavity completely empty
Adding mass and filling the cavity with mineral wool
n: STC rises with mass, cavity absorption and decoupling. Paint and decorations add almost nothing.

q: Which lighting distribution system is inherently efficient because nearly all light is aimed downward?
n: Direct lighting aims 90 to 100% of the light down, so little is lost on the ceiling.

q: Which lighting distribution system requires walls and ceilings finished with high-reflectance surfaces?
n: Indirect lighting sends 90 to 100% of the light up, so walls and ceiling must reflect well.

q: Which lighting system uses a translucent diffuser through which the downward-directed light passes?
n: Semi-indirect lighting sends most light up; the small downward part passes through a translucent bowl.

q: Which lighting system distributes roughly equal amounts of light both upward and downward?
n: Direct-indirect lighting sends light up and down in about equal amounts, with little to the sides.
